name: Forza Horizon 2 (Azimuth)
notes:
Azimuth (almost-there-games.itch.io/azimuth, v0.9.9) is a WRAPPER, not a port: it translates Xbox WinRT calls to Win32 and Xbox D3D11 to desktop D3D12, so the Xbox One build of Forza Horizon 2 runs on a PC. The game never had a PC release. Staged 2026-10-14.

PROTON, NOT NATIVE, AND THAT IS THE SUPPORTED PATH. There is no Linux build; the author lists Windows 10/11 and "Linux through Proton" as the targets and names handheld play as in scope. The binary is x86-64 and references d3d12/d3d11/dxgi/vkd3d/D3DCompiler, so vkd3d-proton does the heavy lifting — a better-placed stack for this AMD handheld than PinyonShift, which targets Vulkan directly and whose docs only qualify NVIDIA. Proton EXPERIMENTAL specifically, per the author.

It carries its own VS2012 runtime (msvcp110/msvcr110 in data/bin), so no vcrun install in the prefix.

THE GATE IS THE GAME EXE'S SHA-256, AND 1.0.0.64 IS HOW YOU GET THE RIGHT ONE. azimuth.exe carries 103 distinct pinned 64-hex hashes and the strings "Game executable hash mismatch" and "Not a folder of a supported game" (both confirmed present in the binary). So the version number is necessary but not sufficient — a differently packaged or re-dumped 1.0.0.64 can still be refused, and the symptom is a hash mismatch rather than anything about the version. The pinned set is also why this recipe can never be generalised to another game: a new title needs a record only the developer can add. Verified from the dump's own Mount/AppxManifest.xml: Identity Name="Anthem" Version="1.0.0.64", DisplayName "Forza Horizon 2", TitleId 1A96545B, Executable Forza_Durango_Release_Final.exe. "Anthem" is FH2's internal package name — the map geometry lives under Mount/media/tracks/anthem/ — so a folder called Anthem_1.0.0.64_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe IS Forza Horizon 2 and is not mislabelled.

LAYOUT MATTERS AND THE EXE SAYS SO. The package folder must be whole: era.vbi + Mount/ + EmbeddedXvd/, all three. EmbeddedXvd is not padding — it holds EmbeddedXvd/Windows/System32/xg_x.dll, the Xbox graphics-tiling library the D3D11.X-to-D3D12 translation needs for placement and XG tiled textures (confirmed present on the staged copy). The game exe inside is Mount/forza_durango_release_final.exe, 55.5 MB — note it is LOWERCASE on disk while AppxManifest.xml declares it mixed-case. On btrfs that is a different path, so never retype it from the manifest; this is the Halo MCC wrong-case bug waiting to happen again. Azimuth refuses anything else with "Not a game folder or a content package: no Mount\AppxManifest.xml", and warns "(copy the whole package folder, not only Mount)". Its own data/ folder must sit beside azimuth.exe or it reports "Azimuth's data folder is missing or incomplete".

WHY THIS TRAVELS. data/azimuth.ini records the game under [title-1a96545b] as folder=Anthem_1.0.0.64_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe — a RELATIVE folder name, no absolute path anywhere in the file. So the staged tree can move between machines unchanged, the same property that makes PinyonShift portable. The exe also accepts --game=DIR for scripted runs, which is the fallback if the ini is ever lost; it is not needed while the ini is intact, and the launcher would be skipped.

Offline only: no Xbox Live, so no multiplayer, clubs or achievements. 0.9.9 pre-release with frequent fixes. There is no in-game quit — exit with the Steam button.

TWO SEPARATE PIPELINE CACHES, and only one is disposable. Do not conflate them. (a) data/bin/azimuth.pipelines, 2.4 MB, format AZMPIPE1, SHIPPED by the author and keyed per game-exe hash — this one is part of the payload, keep it. (b) data/cache/pipelines-<vendor>-<device>-....bin, 87.4 MB, GENERATED and keyed by GPU; the staged one is 10de/2684, an NVIDIA desktop card, so it is dead weight on this AMD handheld and RADV will build its own on first run. Harmless, left in place rather than special-cased. data/cache/translated-*.pack (49.1 MB) is keyed by game, not GPU, so that one should carry over.

The staged azimuth.ini is tuned for the desktop: frame_rate=165, hdr=on, msaax4, resolution=1080. Worth turning down on the handheld — the author reports 720p60 or 1080p30 on a Steam Deck, and the Legion Go 2 is comfortably faster than a Deck, so 1080p60 is a reasonable target rather than a guarantee.

save_paths are NOT verified. Nothing had been saved at staging time, so there was nothing to confirm against. data/titles/1A96545B is the per-title state directory (title id from the manifest) and is the obvious candidate; azimuth.ini is listed alongside it because the graphics configuration is worth keeping even though it is settings rather than a save. If a capture of this recipe comes back empty, that path is wrong — which is the only symptom you get.

EXTRA OPTIONS 0.2.74 REPLACES azimuth-tls.dll, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE INSTALL. RokkuDayo's FH2 Extra Options (GPL-3.0, github.com/RokkuDayo/ForzaHorizon2_ExtraOptions, source linked from its own Read-me.txt) ships two halves: Azimuth/ for this wrapper and Mezcal/ for the other FH2 translation layer. ONLY the Azimuth/ half may be installed here — Mezcal/xg.dll would land next to the game exe in Mount/ on that stack and means nothing to Azimuth, so the recipe names payload/fix/Azimuth/<file> per file and never the extracted root. The mod's azimuth-tls.dll (284672 bytes) re-implements both of the stock DLL's exports (azimuth_tls_attached, azimuth_tls_index) and adds Fh2TweaksStatus; its only import library is KERNEL32 (34 functions, including ReadProcessMemory/VirtualProtect/FlushInstructionCache — it patches the game in memory). The stock DLL is 4608 bytes, sha256 ffa229b6c62228bf6126de6f140c6a70326c536524bec00f9304ac6591805bb7 on the Legion, and is kept as azimuth-tls.dll.gfm-orig; revert restores it byte-for-byte ONLY while the extracted payload is still present. On a fresh clone after a reimage the payload is gitignored and absent, and revert then raises StepError("payload missing: ...") from CopyFiles._pairs BEFORE any restore runs, so .gfm-orig is never consulted (reproduced; cmd_revert never calls fetch.ensure_remote_payloads). Not data loss - the backup is still on disk - but the restore is manual: copy data/bin/azimuth-tls.dll.gfm-orig back over azimuth-tls.dll yourself, or re-fetch the payload first. It is Azimuth's own closed-source file and is NOT ours to redistribute, so that backup is the only copy of it on the device — do not delete .gfm-orig files in data/bin.

FETCHED, NEVER COMMITTED, AND THE TAG IS A ROLLING ONE. The zip is a remote_payload: 698 KB of GPL-3.0 binary that we have no business re-hosting (conveying it would put the source-availability obligation on us; fetching the author's own asset does not). The release tag is literally "Release", so the author replaces assets in place and the file name carries the version — when 0.2.75 lands, this URL either 404s or the pinned sha256 stops matching, and Apply ABORTS BEFORE ANY STEP RUNS because fetch runs first and a FetchError is not optional. The fix is to update url/sha256/size here. A local-payloads copy does NOT rescue that case (fetch never consults the NAS), but it does survive it if the remote_payloads entry is dropped at the same time.

To keep a customised FH2_ExtraOptions.ini or your own Gamerpic.png across re-applies, drop them at <NAS>/_recipes/forza-horizon-2-azimuth/payload/fix/Azimuth/ — payload_path() prefers a local copy per FILE, which is why these are three file-level steps rather than one directory copy. Without that, every re-apply overwrites both with the mod's defaults. Do NOT add an ini_edit step on FH2_ExtraOptions.ini: the shipped file is CRLF and ini_edit rewrites it LF-only, so copy_files would read PARTIAL forever.

Extra Options 0.2.74 UNTESTED on hardware — not yet applied on the Legion as of 2026-10-15. The zip's own Read-me.txt and INI header both say 0.2.73 while the asset is named 0.2.74.

DO NOT RUN APPLY ON THIS RECIPE AGAINST A MACHINE WITH CUSTOM LAUNCH OPTIONS, AND READ THIS FIRST. Verified on the Legion 2026-10-15: the FH2 shortcut carried LaunchOptions "~/.lsfg %command%" (Lossless Scaling frame generation, /home/deck/.lsfg, set up the same evening). This recipe declares no launch_options, so SteamShortcut sets self.launch_options = "" and shortcutsvdf.ensure_shortcut's existing-entry branch calls _set_field(existing, "LaunchOptions", ...) UNCONDITIONALLY - Apply would silently erase it. It also forces AppName back to the recipe's name.

THAT RENAME IS A 42 GB DELETION PATH, and the save guard does NOT stop it. reclaim.scan does by_name = {r.name: r for r in recipes} - keyed on recipe.name ONLY, not all_names. The Legion's ~/.config/gfm/config.json records this game under the FOLDER name "Forza Horizon 2", which does not equal this recipe's name "Forza Horizon 2 (Azimuth)", so by_name.get() returns None and match_names falls back to ["Forza Horizon 2"]. _norm strips non-alphanumerics and _matches is an EXACT match on the result, so forzahorizon2 != forzahorizon2azimuth. Today the shortcut is still literally "Forza Horizon 2" and find_appids returns [3451071415], so the scan reports "kept - still in Steam" and there are zero candidates. Rename it and has_shortcut goes False while shortcut_seen is already latched True -> the 42 GB folder becomes a candidate, and because recipe is None, _saves_safe returns True immediately without ever looking at save_paths. weekly-backup then deletes it UNPROMPTED: cmd_weekly_backup does setattr(self.args, "auto", True) and step 6/6 calls cmd_reclaim, which takes the if auto: branch (chosen = res.candidates, up to MAX_AUTO_BATCH = 3) with no confirmation. The timer fires Sundays 19:00 AEDT. Until reclaim keys on all_names, treat Apply on this recipe as destructive.

NEVER POINT ini_edit AT data/azimuth.ini. It is UTF-16LE with a BOM and CRLF line endings; ini_edit reads and writes encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape" and rebuilds the file with "\n".join(out). surrogateescape means NOTHING RAISES: apply_recipe reports success while writing a raw \n byte that byte-misaligns every following UTF-16 code unit, after which the file no longer decodes as UTF-16 at all and car_detail is unfindable. Reproduced on a copy 2026-10-15 (980 -> 1068 bytes, BOM still intact and therefore misleading). Only the step's own .gfm-bak makes it recoverable. Azimuth's ini and the mod's ini need opposite handling: azimuth.ini is UTF-16LE/CRLF, FH2_ExtraOptions.ini is ASCII/CRLF and the mod's parser refuses UTF-16, anything over 8192 bytes, and any key it does not know.

PROTON IS UNPROVEN FOR THE MOD, AND THERE IS ONE OPEN LINUX FAILURE REPORT. The mod's own BUILD.md says "Linux/Wine execution has not been tested"; "Linux through Proton" is Azimuth's claim, not the mod's. GitHub issue #6 is open, and on 2026-10-15 a commenter on Fedora 44 / Proton 11 / Azimuth 0.9.9 reported the same "Cannot load the native static-TLS helper". Disassembly of azimuth.exe 0.9.9 shows that string is emitted purely because LoadLibraryExW(helper, 0, 0x900) returned NULL - it carries no detail and no GetLastError - so it covers a missing file, a blocked load, a bad mapping or an exception in DllMain equally. The original Windows reporter's cause was Smart App Control, which does not exist on Linux, so the Linux cause is unknown. All 34 of the mod's KERNEL32 imports are real implementations in Wine 11.0 (none stubbed), so there is no known blocker - it is simply untested. Success looks like data/bin/FH2_ExtraOptions.log appearing with "OK: requested tweaks applied in memory."; failure is that dialog or a "REFUSED:" line in the log.

INSTALLED BY HAND ON THE LEGION 2026-10-15 23:01, deliberately NOT via Apply (see the launch-options and reclaim hazards above). The three Azimuth/ files were copied into data/bin, the stock DLL preserved as azimuth-tls.dll.gfm-orig, and car_detail set default -> high with a script that preserves the UTF-16LE BOM and CRLF byte-exactly (azimuth.ini.pre-cardetail is that backup). A pre-mod snapshot of the saves tree, azimuth.ini and the stock DLL is on the NAS at _state/fh2-presave-20261015-222540. That snapshot matters because Azimuth keeps only a 2-DEEP ROLLING WINDOW of save revisions, so two more in-game saves prune the pre-mod state permanently. Before the mod, both revisions verified clean against their commit markers; re-run the same check after playing to find out whether the mod keeps the markers consistent, which is what decides whether removing it later is safe.

STORM ISLAND AND FAST & FURIOUS ARE SEPARATE PACKAGES, BOTH STAGED 2026-10-16. The base game dump contains neither: DLC are their own Xbox packages, which is why the staged tree now holds three sibling package folders beside azimuth.exe. Azimuth 0.9.9 added native support for this ("Storm Island and other content packages load from their own folders, registered per game"), so the third-party FH2 DLC Launcher.exe + fh2core.dll floating around from before 0.9.9 are REDUNDANT - do not install them, and note the author's own "PSA: no support for modded wrapper".

  StormIsland_1.0.0.36_neutral__8wekyb3d8bbwe   3.02 GiB, 149 files - a CONTENT PACKAGE
  Spire_1.0.0.6_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe              14.85 GiB, 1212 files - a separate GAME

A content package has AppxManifest.xml at its ROOT (not under Mount/) declaring <mx:ContentPackage>, and needs NO era.vbi - that belongs to a game image only. Storm Island's manifest declares AllowedProduct Id d1f83f36-a0da-4cb2-9a94-b45822d77fb1, and that GUID is present inside the base game's forza_durango_release_final.exe, which is how the two are matched. Spire is a full game image (era.vbi + Mount/ + EmbeddedXvd/, TitleId 5A9771A4, DisplayName "Forza Horizon 2 Presents Fast & Furious") and the devlog marks it EXPERIMENTAL.

THE WIRING LIVES IN azimuth.ini, WHICH IS ALREADY IN save_paths, so a restore brings it back. content= is a '|'-separated list of content-package FOLDER paths resolved against the directory holding azimuth.exe, space-trimmed, empty entries skipped, capped at 8 (established by disassembling azimuth.exe; Azimuth reads/writes it itself with Get/WritePrivateProfileStringW). A separate game gets its own [title-<id>] section. Current state:
  [title-1a96545b] content=StormIsland_1.0.0.36_neutral__8wekyb3d8bbwe
  [title-5a9771a4] folder=Spire_1.0.0.6_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe
Edit that file ONLY with something that preserves UTF-16LE + BOM + CRLF byte-exactly - never ini_edit, for the reason recorded above. The alternative, and the supported route, is the launcher's own Game page.

The base dump is one file short: media/_library/textures.zip (~45.7 MB, 203 entries) is listed by the game's zipmanifest.xml but absent. It is NOT a stale entry - the exe hardcodes game:\media\_library	extures\ as one of 11 asset mount roots (the other 10 all have content) and 1,554 of 3,674 shipped material files reference that root 3,394 times, with none of the content anywhere in the dump. A complete 1.0.0.64 package is 2,502 files / 42,140,160,011 bytes; ours is 2,501 / 42,094,414,743. Impact is probably cosmetic (shared default/test swatches). Azimuth cannot warn about it: it holds no reference to the game's data files or zipmanifest and logs no asset loads, so a clean azimuth.log proves nothing about dump completeness.

STORM ISLAND CONFIRMED WORKING ON THE LEGION, 2026-10-16. Tony played it; Azimuth logged the mount by name in two separate sessions:
  content package StormIsland 1.0.0.36 from D:\Games\Forza Horizon 2\StormIsland_1.0.0.36_neutral__8wekyb3d8bbwe
So several things that were open are now settled:
 - content= works under Proton on RADV, with a RELATIVE folder name resolved against the directory holding azimuth.exe. The value in azimuth.ini is bare (StormIsland_1.0.0.36_neutral__8wekyb3d8bbwe); Azimuth expanded it to the Wine drive path itself.
 - Azimuth 0.9.9's NATIVE content-package support is real on Linux, so the third-party FH2 DLC Launcher.exe + fh2core.dll are confirmed redundant. Do not install them.
 - car_detail=high took effect: the session line reads "graphics custom (... car_detail=high ...)". That setting was written by a BOM/CRLF-preserving script, never ini_edit.
 - Proton Experimental 11.0-20261014 on AMD Radeon 890M (RADV STRIX1), Wine 11.0, render height 1200 at 16:10, 144 fps cap.

save_paths ARE NOW VERIFIED, not inferred. {game_dir}/data/titles/1A96545B/saves holds real progress: revisions advanced from 0x38/0x39 to 0x6a/0x6b across the session, i.e. roughly fifty saves. Azimuth keeps only the latest TWO revisions, so everything between is already gone from the device - which is exactly why this path is in save_paths and why a capture matters. Captured to the NAS 2026-10-16 with the index whole.

CLEAN INTEGRITY BASELINE, MOD OFF. With the stock azimuth-tls.dll in place, both current revisions verify against their commit markers (5 blobs each, all hashes and sizes matching). That is the reference point: re-run the same check after the Extra Options mod goes back on, and if a revision stops verifying then DisableAzimuthSaveChecksums has let the game write blobs whose markers no longer match, and removing the mod later would leave stock Azimuth rejecting the save.
post_apply_message:
Forza Horizon 2 (Azimuth) added to Steam on Proton Experimental. On first launch point the launcher at the folder holding Mount if it asks — it should already be remembered, since azimuth.ini stores it relatively. Turn the settings down from the desktop defaults (165fps/HDR) before playing on the handheld. No in-game quit: use the Steam button.

Extra Options 0.2.74 is now installed in data/bin.

SET "Car Detail" TO HIGH OR ULTRA in Azimuth's settings. On vanilla car model quality the three cars with real roof animations (BMW Z4 iDrive, Mazda MX-5 2013, Ferrari California) look broken when the roof is toggled. They still look wrong in car meets whatever you set — the game forces LOD1 there, and the mod author is raising that with the Azimuth developer rather than working around it.

Controller bindings:
  D-Pad Down  — autodrive (set a GPS route first; press again, or steer / accelerate / brake / pause, to take control back). F2 on a keyboard.
  Right stick, click  — toggle lights, any car.
  Right stick, hold 3s while stationary  — toggle the roof.

The treasure map is OFF by default. To reveal every bonus board and barn, set UnlockTreasureMap=1 in data/bin/FH2_ExtraOptions.ini inside the game folder. It is effectively one-way: load in and save with it on and the boards stay discovered even after you turn it off. INI keys are read only at startup; everything exposed in the in-game menus is saved separately to FH2_ExtraOptions.dat.

Re-applying this recipe overwrites data/bin/FH2_ExtraOptions.ini and Gamerpic.png with the mod's defaults. To keep your own, put them on the NAS under _recipes/forza-horizon-2-azimuth/payload/fix/Azimuth/ — a local copy wins over the downloaded one.
